subject: Post-call: Vectorization adoption & SDK/Auth next steps

Subject: Post-call: Vectorization adoption & SDK/Auth next steps

Rebecca / Trevor — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Call summary (5 min):
- Primary goal: replace current VecCloud embeddings pipeline for product search & recommendations with Redwood-backed vectors.
- Constraints: existing index (VecCloud) is ~120M vectors, current dims are 1024. Team wants parity on relevance and latency <= 12ms p99 for in-prod queries.

Key technical alignment:
- Dimension candidate: we discussed 1024 (parity) vs 1536 (higher fidelity). Recommended approach: migrate initially at 1024 to reduce index rebuild risk, run A/B with 1536 on a sampled slice.
- Normalization: use L2 unit normalization at index/write time; serve reranker on raw floats and compute cosine during scoring.
- Batching: recommend bulk-upsert batches of 10k-50k vectors for the migration job; for inference, start with client-side batching (64-256) and tune.
- Auth & SDK: plan to use service-account style API key scoped to the HorizonCommerce workspace; SDK integration via our Python client (snippet attached in the proposal).
- Routing/fallback: route search traffic to dedicated Redwood cluster; fallback policy to low-cost quantized variant if latency or capacity SLO breached.
- Structured output & reranker: reranker will return structured JSON (id, score, metadata) and call tool endpoints for enrichment.

Agreed next steps (owners / dates):
1) Redwood to share migration proposal + migration checklist (attached) — Evelyn / today EOD
2) Horizon to provide sample query set and 500k sample vectors (S3 link) — Rebecca / by Fri 2026-09-18
3) Tech deep-dive: Karthik + Marissa to run a perf matrix (1024 vs 1536, batch sizes 64/128/256) and share numbers — Karthik / by 2026-09-16
4) Security touchpoint: Marissa to confirm token scoping + retention policy items and SOC2 pointer — Marissa / by 2026-09-20

Attachments: horizon-vector-proposal.pdf (proposal + sample SDK snippets), arch-sketch.png (draft routing + fallback), migration-checklist.md (checklist stub).

If anything above is off, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll treat this as the working plan and kick off the migration experiments on Thursday.

— Evelyn

Subject: Re: Post-call: Vectorization adoption & SDK/Auth next steps — bench notes + early recommendations

Evelyn / team / Rebecca — quick preliminary findings from the micro-bench and my recommendations. I used the 50k sample subset Rebecca uploaded and ran Redwood local-cluster tests. Full bench doc is on Drive (link in metadata).

Summary (early):
- Dim selection: 1536 gives a modest (3–6%) MAP improvement on our relevance testset over 1024, but increases raw storage by ~50% for float32. Quantized int8 reduces size ~4x with ~2–4% relevance delta vs float32 depending on reranker.
- Storage: ~1M vectors @ 1024 float32 ~= 3.9 GB; @1536 float32 ~= 5.8 GB. Int8 quantized profiles reduce to ~1.0–1.6 GB per 1M depending on per-dim packing.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for a dedicated NVIDIA A10 node (Redwood runtime):
  * 1024 dims, batch=64 -> p50 2.4ms / p95 6.1ms / p99 9.8ms
  * 1536 dims, batch=64 -> p50 3.1ms / p95 7.9ms / p99 12.6ms
  * Larger batches increase throughput but add ~0.5–2ms to tail latency; recommend starting with batch=64–128 for user-facing search.
- Normalization: L2 normalization at write time simplifies cosine ops and reduces per-query compute; we see no relevance penalty.

Operational recommendations:
1) Phase 1 (low risk): ingest Horizon vectors at 1024 to match current index; run A/B with 1536 on sample slice (no traffic shift for first 48h).
2) Phase 2 (scale): if 1536 shows >3% improvement on business KPIs, plan full rebuild on a rolling index with streaming backfill. Expect backfill throughput ~200k vectors/hour with our current ingest pipeline; parallelize across 8 workers to hit ~1.6M/hour.
3) Fallback/routing: configure smart routing — prefer dedicated cluster (prod), fallback to a quantized variant in the same region if node-level p99 > 200ms or error rate > 0.5%.

SDK snippet (Python):
# sample
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="redwood-svc-xxxx", workspace="horizon")
# upload (batch)
client.vectors.upsert([{"id":"p1","vector": [0.1, ...], "meta": {"sku":"A123"}}], batch_size=128)
# query + rerank tool call
resp = client.vectors.query("best-match-rich", queries=[[0.2, ...]], top_k=10, reranker=True)
# resp is JSON: [{"id":"...","score":0.92,"meta":{...}}]

Next steps: I’ll push the detailed bench spreadsheet to the Drive link and start drafting the migration checklist (will attach migration-checklist.md). Marissa — if you can confirm the token scoping options, I’ll include the precise auth steps.
